answer.rationale: Finance's 18% mandate can't be met by the incumbent, who has refused to reopen price, and the contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, forcing a decision now. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the cost mandate, and memory_c2 records fast onboarding and accurate invoicing, but that record says nothing about delivery reliability or performance under sustained full-volume load—critical given the line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer. I verified memory_c2 to check for any suppressed reliability detail before committing capital to a full switch; barring stronger evidence there, I'm treating the vendor's delivery track record at scale as unproven. Rather than an all-at-once primary switch, a guarded initial rollout (partial volume or phased cutover) lets us capture the cost benefit while retaining the incumbent or manual buffer as fallback until the new vendor proves it can hold committed volume without slippage. Second-sourcing (memory_c3) and renegotiation (memory_c4) don't resolve the 14-day expiry or the mandate on their own this cycle, and deferral isn't viable with a hard contract deadline.
